question: Which tense is mainly used in the passage?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Past Simple**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage primarily narrates a series of completed actions that took place on a specific morning in the past, which is the core function of the **Past Simple** tense.
 
• Most of the main verbs in the text follow the past simple structure: **"destroyed," "worked," "helped," "watched,"** and **"handled."**
 
• The phrase **"the market was ruined"** also employs the past simple, specifically in the passive voice, to describe the state of the market after the fire.
 
• The use of specific time markers like **"early on Sunday morning"** further confirms the requirement for the past simple tense to describe finished events.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect:** This tense is used at the very end of the passage ("has promised") to link a past action to the present, but it is not the dominant tense used to describe the fire itself.
 
• **Future Perfect:** This tense (e.g., "will have destroyed") describes an action that will be completed before a specific point in the future. It does not appear in this historical report.
 
• **Past Continuous:** This tense (e.g., "was burning") would be used to describe an action that was ongoing at a specific moment in the past. While the fire was an ongoing event, the passage uses simple forms to report the facts.
